title: A frontier AI lab files a public S-1 and prices its IPO by Q2 2027
body: The frontier-lab path to public markets turned concrete this week. Anthropic confidentially filed a draft Form S-1 with the SEC on June 1 - on the back of a $65B round at a $965B post-money valuation and an annualized revenue run-rate that crossed $47B (more than tripled since February) - explicitly setting up an IPO that pits it against OpenAI, which is targeting a raise of at least $60B at a valuation of up to $1 trillion and is expected to list by year's end. The ceiling for how much public-market capital a single high-multiple technology name can absorb just reset: on June 11 SpaceX priced 555.6 million shares at $135 apiece to raise about $75B, the largest IPO in history, demonstrating live appetite for an outsized private-tech debut. The forward thesis is that this confidential, paper-stage maneuvering converts into an actual public offering. The concrete, falsifiable landing: by Q2 2027 at least one of the two largest labs - Anthropic or OpenAI - publicly files a non-confidential Form S-1 (or its F-1 / 424B equivalent), sets a price range or final per-share terms, and prices the offering ahead of a first trade on a US exchange (NYSE or Nasdaq), confirmed via the SEC EDGAR public filing plus an on-record pricing press release or exchange listing notice. The doesn't-count set is explicit: a confidential or draft S-1 alone (the June 1 status) does not count; neither does a further private round, a directing-bank mandate, an analyst report, an exchange reservation of a ticker, or an indicative range that is withdrawn before pricing. What counts is a public registration that proceeds to set terms and price - the moment the lab commits to selling shares to public investors at a stated price. The counter-risk is that a private-market round at SpaceX-scale valuations, or a regulatory or market-window stall, lets both labs stay private through mid-2027, leaving the confidential filing as the furthest either gets.

reasoning.because: June 1: Anthropic confidentially filed a draft S-1 ($965B post-money); OpenAI prepping its listing
reasoning.given: SpaceX's June 11 $75B pricing at $135/share reset the ceiling for public capital in one tech name
reasoning.so_that: Anthropic or OpenAI converts a draft filing into a public, non-confidential S-1 that sets terms and prices an IPO
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; Anthropic or OpenAI public S-1 + priced offering on NYSE/Nasdaq
reasoning.plain_language: Anthropic secretly filed to go public and OpenAI is getting ready too; soon one of them will openly sell shares at a set price.

summary: Anthropic confidentially filed a draft S-1 on June 1 ($965B post-money), OpenAI is preparing its own listing, and SpaceX's $75B June 11 pricing proved public-market appetite. Expect Anthropic or OpenAI to file a non-confidential S-1 and price an IPO by Q2 2027; a confidential draft does not count.
